protections: P1 (advisory): the AuthZ request plugin must see the request body the daemon will act on; if it cannot be shown (too large or skipped), the request must not be forwarded as if it were bodyless (authz.go:71-116).

P2 (same concept, different decision): which requests get their body shown to the plugin is decided by the client-supplied Content-Type header, not by whether the handler will parse the body as JSON (authz.go:173-193).
P3 (response side): AuthZResponse must decide before response data reaches the client (response.go:120-130, middleware.go:81-102).

evidence: pkg/authorization/authz.go:151-153 (Peek succeeds on an oversized body: logs a warning, returns nil data, request continues)
pkg/authorization/authz.go:91 (nil body put into the plugin request)
pkg/authorization/authz.go:102-113 (plugins run on the empty body; allow lets the request through)
pkg/authorization/middleware.go:76-85 (handler then reads the full body)

traps.reason_to_dismiss: The skip logic lives in drainBody (authz.go:151-153). Making drainBody fail closed looks like a complete fix, but a declared Content-Length >= 1MB never reaches drainBody.
evidence: pkg/authorization/authz.go:73 (`r.ContentLength < maxBodySize` silently skips the drain for declared-length bodies; body stays nil)
pkg/authorization/authz.go:18 (maxBodySize = 1MB)

traps.reason_to_dismiss: Showing the plugin only application/json bodies is the documented design, and handlers such as container create enforce Content-Type themselves (container_routes.go:450). A solver can assume a non-JSON request body is never parsed as JSON.
evidence: pkg/authorization/authz.go:187-192 (body withheld unless the client's Content-Type parses as application/json)
api/server/router/swarm/cluster_routes.go:194-211 (createService decodes r.Body as JSON with no CheckForJSON, then calls CreateService)
api/server/router/swarm/cluster_routes.go:22-29 (initCluster same)
api/server/router/plugin/plugin_routes.go:132-141 (pullPlugin decodes privileges from the body with no Content-Type check)
api/server/httputils/httputils.go:50-65 (CheckForJSON exists but only some routes call it, e.g. container_routes.go:450, exec.go:41, network_routes.go:214)
pkg/authorization/authz.go:73 (the size check is currently gated by sendBody, so non-JSON bodies are never inspected)
api/server/router/build/build_routes.go:213 (build context tar streamed from r.Body, routinely >1MB)
api/server/router/image/image_routes.go:181 (image load streams r.Body)
api/server/router/container/copy.go:144 (PUT archive streams r.Body)
Coupled value: the T1/T2 fix must reject only bodies the plugin would have been shown. A blanket 'deny any body >1MB' breaks these routes.

traps.reason_to_dismiss: Streaming and hijacked responses (attach, logs, events, pulls) cannot be buffered whole, so early flushing is deliberate design, not a bug.
evidence: pkg/authorization/response.go:50 (64KB buffer)
pkg/authorization/response.go:125-127 (a buffer overflow flushes the response to the client before AuthZResponse runs)
pkg/authorization/response.go:146-149 (Hijack flushes and passes the connection through)
pkg/authorization/middleware.go:85-102 (AuthZResponse runs only after the handler has finished writing)

traps.reason_to_dismiss: Duplicate request headers are unusual, and the daemon does not normally act on them.
evidence: pkg/authorization/authz.go:203-205 (multi-valued headers flattened so the plugin sees the LAST value)
pkg/authorization/authz.go:187 (sendBody uses header.Get, the FIRST value)
api/server/router/swarm/cluster_routes.go:205 (handler reads the 'version' header with Get, the first value)

traps.reason_to_dismiss: The handler already returned an error, or the plugin was removed by the operator, so there is nothing to authorize.
evidence: pkg/authorization/middleware.go:99 (AuthZResponse deny ignored when errD != nil)
pkg/authorization/middleware.go:91-95 (response authorization skipped if the plugin list emptied while the handler ran)

masking: Fix A (authz.go:73 `r.ContentLength > 0 || isChunked(r)`) sends chunked bodies into drainBody. An oversized chunked body then hits the nil-body skip at authz.go:151-153 (T1). A closed the zero-length route without changing the oversized skip, which already existed.

conflicts.what: Failing closed on any body above maxBodySize (in drainBody, or by dropping the sendBody gate at authz.go:73) rejects build contexts, image loads and archive uploads larger than 1MB (build_routes.go:213, image_routes.go:181, copy.go:144).

Sending the body to the plugin whatever its Content-Type, as a T3 fix, would feed tar streams into the 1MB peek. Combined with a fail-closed T1 fix, that denies every large build or load. T3 has to be fixed per route (CheckForJSON on JSON-decoding handlers) or by showing the body without failing closed for non-JSON types.
Buffering the whole response before AuthZResponse breaks streaming and hijacked endpoints (attach, logs, events, build output).

fairness_risks: Request bodies over 1MB with a non-JSON Content-Type (build, images/load, PUT archive) must keep working. A rule that denies oversized bodies has to be scoped to bodies the plugin would have been shown.
JSON request bodies under 1MB, chunked or with a declared length, must still reach the plugin and the daemon unchanged (the A behaviour at authz.go:73-79).
Adding CheckForJSON to swarm/plugin routes for T3 rejects clients that send JSON with no Content-Type. The in-tree client always sets it (client/request.go:86); third-party clients might not.
T5 cannot be tested without contradicting streaming responses; keep it out of hidden tests.

design.why: Best available stack: the advisory route covered at both sites (drainBody and the Content-Length gate), plus the coupled must-keep-working large non-JSON bodies (mimo-type T4) and the Content-Type gate on routes without CheckForJSON (deepseek-type T3). Only 2 independent groups are testable, below the 3-5 bar. T5 contradicts streaming (fairness). T6 and T7 are low-impact and give weak tests. Usable as a 2-group pair only, so rejected as a 3+ stack.

unverified: Content of the B fix e89edb19ad7d (assumed: fail closed / deny when the JSON body exceeds maxBodySize); not present in the pinned tree.

That the `r.ContentLength < maxBodySize` clause and the drainBody skip predate A's commits (git blame not run); the b_in_code_a_wrote=false answer rests on the szz_status H3b-elsewhere label and the A commit message.
Upstream has not classified T3 (Content-Type-gated body hiding on swarm/plugin routes) as a vulnerability; it is inferred from authz.go:187-192 plus handlers that skip CheckForJSON.
T6 is a theoretical exploit path; no handler found that turns the first/last header mismatch into a privileged action.
